subject: general
question: How many Indian Institutes of Technology were started under the First Five-Year Plan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the First Five-Year Plan in India, **five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) were established** to promote higher technical education and research.
 
• The first IIT was **established in Kharagpur in 1951**, which set the precedent for others to follow.
 
• Subsequently, four more IITs were established in Bombay (1958), Madras (1959), Kanpur (1959), and Delhi (1961).
 
• The IITs were modeled after the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and were intended to train scientists and engineers to support India's economic and industrial development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)**

 
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951 by India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The plan focused on the agriculture sector, aiming to enhance food production and reduce import dependency.
 
• It aimed to address the immediate need for food security, employment, and infrastructure development in the country.
 
• The successful implementation of this plan laid the foundation for subsequent economic planning and development in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs)**
 
 
• IITs are autonomous public technical and research universities located across India.
 
• They are governed by the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961 which declares them as institutions of national importance.
 
• IITs offer undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs in various engineering, technology, science, and management disciplines.
 
• They are known for their rigorous academic standards, world-class faculty, and significant contributions to research and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Technical Education in India**
 
 
• Technical education in India encompasses training and education in the fields of engineering, technology, applied sciences, and management.
 
• Institutions such as IITs, National Institutes of Technology (NITs), and Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIITs) play a pivotal role in this domain.
 
• These institutions aim to provide quality education, foster research and innovation, and contribute to the technological and economic advancement of the country.
 
• The emphasis is on creating a skilled workforce that can meet the demands of industry and drive the nation's growth.
